source: Independent Python port of the Magfit 6-degree spherical-harmonic expansion in src/lib/propagation/ionosphere/modip.ts (the same G, H and CT tables, the same truncated D2R = 0.0174532925 and the same 2.8 * sqrt(...) gyrofrequency scaling). No ITU file is reproduced or redistributed; the ITU reference build is a parity benchmark, never a dependency.
quantity: Longitudinal gyrofrequency fL = |fH sin(dip)| of ITU-R P.533-14 equation (20), MHz.
notes: absorption_delta_*_db is the change in equation (20) loss when fL replaces the absorption leaf's declared 1.2 MHz scalar. Equation (20) divides by (f + fL)^2, so the numerator cancels and the change is exactly 20 log10((f + 1.2) / (f + fL)) dB. Positive means the corrected fL absorbs more than the stand-in. longitudinal_gyrofrequency_300km_mhz is the same quantity at the height the CCIR map's modip coordinate is defined at, recorded so a later refactor cannot quietly reuse the 300 km field because it is already on the state object.

cases.description: Mid latitude, dip close to the 1.2 MHz scalar the absorption leaf declares, so the correction is near zero and this case alone cannot prove the wiring works.
Near the magnetic dip equator, where sin(dip) collapses and the correction is at its largest.
High northern dip, where fL exceeds 1.2 MHz and the sign of the correction flips.
Southern hemisphere, negative dip: a lost Math.abs or a sign error in dipRad shows up here.
